MLV port assessment: executed evidence

Source: ASSESSMENT_EVIDENCE.md

Date: 2026-10-25. Inputs were synthetic. No R port or performance benchmark exists yet.

Source revisions and scope

Reference Observed local checkout Git HEAD
MATLAB MLV toolbox MLV_toolbox/ f12418a5e03c2f38e222fed1dffccf42b227cd29
Python MLV port vendor/pyMLV/ 14b3183b91146b1021eb7ef97db75ad703b06832

These are the paths observed during the assessment. The user is arranging the vendoring layout; refresh the paths before implementation. Both tracked-file status checks were empty after the probes. The probes did not modify either checkout. Git emitted sandbox temporary-cache warnings but returned status 0. No restricted image datasets were read.

Octave availability

Octave 11.1.0 and image 2.20.0 were found locally. After pkg load image:

  • Available: bwdist, bwmorph, bwareaopen, rgb2gray, imbinarize.
  • Missing from this installed environment: smoothdata, knnsearch, insertShape, xmlread, imsegsam.
  • A 5-by-7 single-feature bwdist probe returned single-precision distances and uint32 nearest-feature indices. The feature distance was 0 and a diagonal neighbor distance was approximately sqrt(2).
  • Installed bwmorph.m, lines 191–197, explicitly documents that its skel result differs from MATLAB on the documented circles example. Therefore Octave execution is valuable evidence, with backend-specific qualification for morphology and tie-sensitive downstream calculations.

The initial sandboxed help-rendering command ended in a temporary-file error after the capability and distance checks completed. A later adapted MAT attempt using the octave GUI wrapper failed in Qt startup (missing cocoa platform plugin, child exit -6); octave-cli avoided that failure.

Unmodified MATLAB source run under Octave

The following synthetic setup was passed through upstream functions:

pkg load image;
addpath("MLV_toolbox/MLVcode");
v = struct();
v.imsize = [30,20];
v.numContours = 1;
v.contours = {[1,1,11,1]};
v.originalImage = "synthetic";
v.lineMethod = "synthetic";
v = computeContourProperties(v, {"orientation","length","curvature"});
[v,h,b] = getHorizontalVerticalStats(v);
v.junctions = [];
[v,jh,jb] = getJunctionStats(v);

w = v;
w.imsize = [30,30];
w.numContours = 3;
w.contours = {[1,1,5,1], [1,10,5,10], [1,20,3,20]};
w = computeContourProperties(w);
[top,bottom] = splitLDbyProperties(w, "length", 0.5);

m = ones(25,35);
m(4:22,8) = 0;
m(4:22,27) = 0;
% The original computeMAT call was wrapped in try/catch to retain its error.
mat = computeMAT(m,28);

Observed transcript (process exit 0 because the MAT exception was caught):

OMP: Warning #179: Function Can't set size of /tmp file failed:
core: length=10 orientation=0 curvature=0
horizontal histogram: total=0 expected_length=10 bins=8
empty junction angles: histogram_length=5 centers_length=8
split: source_length=10 top_length=8 bottom_length=2
MAT_BLOCKED: syntax error near line 67, column 67 in file /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/mlvtoolbox/MLV_toolbox/MLVcode/computeGradientVectorField.m

Interpretation:

  • The analytical contour case succeeds: length 10, orientation 0, curvature 0.
  • The horizontal/vertical histogram loses the full segment length at its upper boundary.
  • Empty junction-angle values and bin centers have inconsistent lengths.
  • Sorting the three contours by length and splitting at 0.5 retains 80% in the top group, exceeding the nominal 50% budget. The earlier arithmetic-only illustration did not apply this sort; this function-level result supersedes it.
  • The original distance-field source contains two jj++m_Neighbors8 expressions. Octave rejects this syntax before evaluating the function.

Minimal Octave adaptation

A temporary copy of computeGradientVectorField.m replaced only the two jj++m_Neighbors8 expressions with jj + m_Neighbors8. In MATLAB, the former expression denotes addition with unary plus; the explicit addition avoids Octave’s parsing ambiguity. The original vendor file was unchanged. The temporary directory was removed by Python’s TemporaryDirectory context.

Reproduction driver:

from pathlib import Path
import tempfile, subprocess
src=Path('MLV_toolbox/MLVcode/computeGradientVectorField.m')
text=src.read_text()
assert text.count('jj++m_Neighbors8')==2
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='mlv-octave-assessment-') as td:
    (Path(td)/src.name).write_text(text.replace('jj++m_Neighbors8','jj + m_Neighbors8'))
    expr='pkg load image; addpath("'+str(src.parent.resolve())+'"); addpath("'+td+'","-begin"); fprintf("runtime=%s image=2.20.0 adaptation=two jj++ to jj + occurrences\\n",version); m=ones(25,35); m(4:22,8)=0; m(4:22,27)=0; try, mat=computeMAT(m,28); fprintf("adapted MAT: skeleton_pixels=%d finite_dist=%d finite_AOF=%d shape=%dx%d\\n",nnz(mat.skeleton),all(isfinite(mat.distance_map(:))),all(isfinite(mat.AOF(:))),size(mat.skeleton,1),size(mat.skeleton,2)); catch err, fprintf("ADAPTED_MAT_BLOCKED: %s\\n",err.message); exit(2); end;'
    proc=subprocess.run(['octave-cli','--quiet','--no-history','--eval',expr],capture_output=True,text=True)
    print(proc.stdout,end=''); print(proc.stderr,end='')
    print('process_exit='+str(proc.returncode))
    raise SystemExit(proc.returncode)

Observed transcript:

runtime=11.1.0 image=2.20.0 adaptation=two jj++ to jj + occurrences
adapted MAT: skeleton_pixels=44 finite_dist=1 finite_AOF=1 shape=25x35
process_exit=0

This demonstrates that the AOF/MAT construction path executes on one small synthetic image with a documented syntax adaptation. It does not validate the skeleton against MATLAB, exercise branch scores/projection, or establish performance.

Python assessment

Python 3.14.7 and NumPy 2.4.3 were used for the probe. SciPy and tqdm were discoverable; cv2 and skimage were not installed in this Python environment. No dependencies were installed and the full Python pipeline was not run.

Static tree/module inspection found 60 top-level Python modules, 52 with same-named MATLAB core counterparts, plus eight Python helpers. No pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg, automated test directory or GitHub workflow was identified in the pinned tree. Name overlap does not establish functional coverage.

Missing local imports include smoothData, diff, fitLineSegments, and GetConSeg. The Python gradient-field function loads outerBoundaryOriginal.mat and opens diagnostic plots. These are source-level findings, not a failed full-pipeline run.

An actual call to computeOrientation with this subpixel segment:

contours = np.empty((1, 1), dtype=object)
contours[0, 0] = np.array([[1.1, 1.1, 1.9, 1.9]], dtype=float)
v = {"numContours": np.array([[1]]), "contours": contours}
observed = computeOrientation(v)["orientations"][0][0]
expected = np.degrees(np.arctan2(-0.8, 0.8)) % 360

returned 0 degrees; the analytical result is 315 degrees. The implementation casts all endpoints to int32 before subtraction. It therefore discards the subpixel geometry in this example.

Probe receipt:

{"python": "3.14.7", "numpy": "2.4.3", "core_py_files": 60, "missing_local_imports": [{"file": "getBranchDerivative.py", "module": "smoothData"}, {"file": "getBranchDerivative.py", "module": "diff"}, {"file": "computeMATpropertyPerBranch.py", "module": "fitLineSegments"}, {"file": "computeMATpropertyPerBranch.py", "module": "smoothData"}, {"file": "computeMATpropertyPerBranch.py", "module": "diff"}, {"file": "traceSkeleton.py", "module": "GetConSeg"}], "subpixel_orientation": {"input": [[1.1, 1.1, 1.9, 1.9]], "observed": 0.0, "expected": 315.0}}

Further source-level risks, not executed here:

  • extract2DSkeletonFromBinaryImage aliases skeletonImage = fluxImage and then thresholds in place, overwriting the flux values returned as AOF.
  • It overrides the calculated component threshold with the constant 100.
  • computeMATpropertyPerBranch changes MATLAB local derivative magnitudes to cumulative sums, and its taper branch references newddR before assignment.
  • Several functions depend on MATLAB-file nesting conventions and mix coordinate/index representations.

These examples make pyMLV useful for ideas, adapters, and selected differential tests, while each numerical path needs its own correctness evidence.

Boundaries

No package tests, cross-language end-to-end parity checks, speedups, memory benchmarks, scientific method improvements, hosted CI or distribution checks are claimed. The demonstrated differences should become regression tests in the R implementation. Passing the adapted MAT smoke is evidence of executability on this input only.
